title: Should You Switch Doors?
subtitle: 該不該換門？蒙提霍爾問題與機率直覺的陷阱
source: 原創議題文章；依 Wikipedia〈Monty Hall problem〉所整理之 Selvin（1975）、vos Savant（1990–91）、Tierney（1991）、Herbranson & Schroeder（2010）等資料核對，2026-10-22

beginner.title: Three Doors, One Car
paras: Imagine you are on a TV game show. There are three doors. Behind one door is a new car. Behind the other two are goats. You choose a door — say, door 1. You hope the car is behind it. This puzzle is named after Monty Hall, the host of an American game show called Let’s Make a Deal.
想像你參加一個電視益智節目。台上有三扇門，其中一扇門後面是一輛新車，另外兩扇門後面是山羊。你選了一扇門——假設是 1 號門。你希望車子就在它後面。這道謎題以蒙提．霍爾命名，他是美國益智節目《來做筆交易吧》的主持人。

Then the host, who knows where the car is, opens door 3. There is a goat behind it. Now he asks you: “Do you want to change to door 2?” What should you do? Most people say it does not matter. They think each door now has a 50% chance.
接著，知道車子在哪裡的主持人打開了 3 號門，門後是一隻山羊。這時他問你：「你要不要換成 2 號門？」你該怎麼做？大多數人說沒差，他們認為現在每扇門都有 50% 的機會。

Surprisingly, you should switch. If you switch, you win the car two times out of three. If you stay, you win only one time out of three. Why? When you first chose, you had only a 1 in 3 chance. The host’s choice did not change that. So the other door now has a 2 in 3 chance.
出人意料的是，你應該換。如果你換門，三次裡有兩次會贏得車子；如果你不換，三次裡只有一次會贏。為什麼？你一開始選的時候，只有三分之一的機會。主持人的選擇並沒有改變這一點，所以另一扇門現在有三分之二的機會。

In 1990, a writer called Marilyn vos Savant explained this answer in a magazine. About 10,000 readers wrote to say she was wrong. Nearly 1,000 of them had PhDs! Even a famous mathematician did not believe it until he saw a computer test.
1990 年，一位名叫瑪莉蓮．沃斯．莎凡特的作家在雜誌上解釋了這個答案。大約一萬名讀者寫信說她錯了，其中將近一千人擁有博士學位！甚至有一位知名數學家，直到看了電腦模擬才相信。

Here is the funny part: pigeons learn to switch faster than people do. Our feelings about chance are often wrong. When a puzzle seems easy, it is a good idea to test it. You can try it yourself with three cups and a coin.
最好笑的是：鴿子學會換門的速度比人類還快。我們對機率的直覺常常是錯的。當一個謎題看起來很簡單時，最好親自測試看看。你可以用三個杯子和一枚硬幣自己試試。

intermediate.title: Should You Switch Doors?
paras: In 1990, a reader sent a puzzle to Marilyn vos Savant’s “Ask Marilyn” column in Parade magazine. You are on a game show with three doors. Behind one is a car; behind the others, goats. You pick door 1. The host, who knows what is behind every door, opens door 3 to reveal a goat. He then asks whether you want to switch to door 2. Is it to your advantage to switch?
1990 年，一位讀者寄了一道謎題給《Parade》雜誌瑪莉蓮．沃斯．莎凡特的「問瑪莉蓮」專欄。你參加一個有三扇門的益智節目，一扇門後是車，另外兩扇後是山羊。你選了 1 號門。知道每扇門後面是什麼的主持人打開 3 號門，露出一隻山羊，然後問你要不要換成 2 號門。換門對你有利嗎？

Most people feel sure the answer is no: with two doors left, the chances must be fifty-fifty. Vos Savant said you should switch. Under the standard assumptions — that the host always opens a door, always reveals a goat and always offers a switch — switching wins two-thirds of the time, while staying wins only one-third.
大多數人很確定答案是否定的：只剩兩扇門，機會一定是一半一半。沃斯．莎凡特卻說你應該換。在標準假設下——主持人一定會開門、一定會露出山羊、一定會讓你換——換門贏的機率是三分之二，不換只有三分之一。

The key is that the host’s action is not random. When you first choose, there is a two-thirds chance that the car is behind one of the other doors. The host, who must avoid the car, removes one wrong option from that group, so the whole two-thirds chance moves to the one door he leaves closed. Vos Savant offered a vivid version: imagine a million doors, and the host opens every one except your choice and door 777,777. You would switch pretty quickly.
關鍵在於，主持人的行動不是隨機的。你一開始選的時候，車子有三分之二的機率在另外兩扇門之一後面。必須避開車子的主持人，從那一組裡拿掉一個錯誤選項，所以整整三分之二的機率，就轉移到他留著沒開的那扇門上。沃斯．莎凡特提出一個生動的版本：想像有一百萬扇門，主持人把除了你選的那扇和 777,777 號門以外的門全部打開。你會很快就換門。

Her answer caused an uproar. About 10,000 readers, including nearly 1,000 with PhDs, wrote to the magazine, most of them insisting she was wrong. Paul Erdős, one of the most productive mathematicians in history, remained unconvinced until he was shown a computer simulation. The puzzle had actually been posed earlier, by the statistician Steve Selvin in 1975. Even when given explanations and formal proofs, many readers still refused to accept the answer, and the argument reached the front page of The New York Times.
她的答案引發一片譁然。大約一萬名讀者寫信給雜誌，其中將近一千人有博士學位，大多數人堅稱她錯了。史上最多產的數學家之一保羅．艾狄胥，一直到看了電腦模擬才被說服。其實這道謎題更早就有人提出過，是統計學家史蒂夫．塞爾文在 1975 年提出的。即使看了解釋和正式證明，許多讀者仍拒絕接受這個答案，這場爭論甚至登上了《紐約時報》頭版。

Strangely, pigeons that face the problem repeatedly quickly learn to always switch, while humans often keep resisting. The lesson is not that people are bad at maths, but that our intuitions about probability can be confidently wrong. When a problem seems obvious, testing it — with cups, cards or a simple computer program — is often the fastest way to the truth.
奇怪的是，反覆面對這個問題的鴿子很快就學會一律換門，人類卻常常一直抗拒。這個教訓不是人類數學不好，而是我們對機率的直覺，可能錯得理直氣壯。當一個問題看起來理所當然時，動手測試——用杯子、撲克牌或一個簡單的電腦程式——往往是通往真相最快的路。

advanced.title: Confidently Wrong: Probability and Intuition
paras: Few puzzles have humbled as many clever people as the Monty Hall problem. Named after the original host of the American game show Let’s Make a Deal, it was first posed by the statistician Steve Selvin in a 1975 letter to The American Statistician. It became famous in 1990, when a reader’s version appeared in Marilyn vos Savant’s “Ask Marilyn” column in Parade magazine: a contestant chooses one of three doors, behind one of which is a car; the host, who knows where the car is, opens another door to reveal a goat and offers the contestant the chance to switch.
很少有謎題像蒙提霍爾問題一樣，讓這麼多聰明人吃了苦頭。它以美國益智節目《來做筆交易吧》的首任主持人命名，最早由統計學家史蒂夫．塞爾文在 1975 年寫給《美國統計學家》期刊的信中提出。1990 年，一位讀者的版本出現在《Parade》雜誌瑪莉蓮．沃斯．莎凡特的「問瑪莉蓮」專欄，從此聲名大噪：參賽者從三扇門中選一扇，其中一扇後面有車；知道車在哪的主持人打開另一扇門露出山羊，並讓參賽者有機會換門。

Vos Savant’s answer — that the contestant should switch — provoked an extraordinary reaction. Approximately 10,000 readers, including nearly 1,000 with PhDs, wrote to the magazine, most of them claiming she was wrong. Even when given explanations, simulations and formal proofs, many still refused to accept the result. The mathematician Paul Erdős reportedly remained unconvinced until he saw a computer simulation, and the controversy reached the front page of The New York Times.
沃斯．莎凡特的答案——參賽者應該換門——引發了非比尋常的反應。大約一萬名讀者寫信給雜誌，其中將近一千人擁有博士學位，大多數人宣稱她錯了。即使看了解釋、模擬和正式證明，許多人仍拒絕接受這個結果。據說數學家保羅．艾狄胥一直到看了電腦模擬才被說服，這場爭議還登上了《紐約時報》頭版。

Under the standard assumptions, the mathematics is not difficult. The contestant’s first choice has a one-third chance of being correct, which means there is a two-thirds chance that the car lies behind one of the other two doors. Crucially, the host’s action is constrained: he knows where the car is and will never reveal it. By opening a losing door from the unchosen pair, he concentrates that entire two-thirds probability on the remaining closed door. Switching therefore wins with probability two-thirds; staying, one-third. Vos Savant’s million-door version makes the logic almost visible: if the host opens every door except yours and one other, the other door is plainly the one he was avoiding.

在標準假設下，數學並不難。參賽者第一次選擇正確的機率是三分之一，也就是說，車子有三分之二的機率在另外兩扇門之一後面。關鍵在於主持人的行動受到限制：他知道車在哪，而且絕不會打開那扇門。他從沒被選的兩扇門中打開一扇輸的門，就把那整整三分之二的機率集中到剩下那扇關著的門上。因此，換門獲勝的機率是三分之二；不換是三分之一。沃斯．莎凡特的百萬扇門版本，幾乎讓這個邏輯一目了然：如果主持人打開除了你和另一扇以外的所有門，那另一扇顯然就是他刻意避開的那扇。

Why, then, is the error so persistent? Part of the answer is that people treat the two remaining doors as equivalent, ignoring the information carried by the host’s constrained choice. Another part is that the popular wording leaves important conditions unstated. As critics noted at the time, the Parade version did not explicitly say that the host always opens a door and always offers a switch; if he could choose whether to do so, the probabilities might differ. Careful reasoning, in other words, depends not only on calculation but on stating assumptions precisely.
那麼，為什麼這個錯誤如此頑固？部分原因是，人們把剩下的兩扇門當成等價的，忽略了主持人受限的選擇所帶來的資訊。另一部分原因是，流行的說法沒有講清楚重要的條件。正如當時的批評者指出，《Parade》的版本並沒有明確說主持人一定會開門、一定會讓人換門；如果他可以自行決定要不要這麼做，機率就可能不同。換句話說，嚴謹的推理不只取決於計算，也取決於精確地陳述假設。

Perhaps the most humbling detail comes from animal research. Pigeons repeatedly exposed to the problem rapidly learn to always switch, whereas humans tend not to. Learning from experience, the birds are untroubled by the conviction that “it must be fifty-fifty”. The cognitive scientist Massimo Piattelli-Palmarini observed that no other statistical puzzle comes so close to fooling everyone. The lasting lesson is that confidence is not evidence: when intuition and calculation disagree, the sensible response is to test the claim rather than defend the feeling.
也許最令人汗顏的細節來自動物研究。反覆面對這個問題的鴿子，很快就學會一律換門，人類卻往往不會。鳥兒從經驗中學習，不受「一定是一半一半」這種信念的干擾。認知科學家馬西莫．皮亞泰利－帕爾馬里尼指出，沒有其他統計謎題能如此接近騙倒所有人。這個問題留下的教訓是：自信不等於證據。當直覺與計算衝突時，明智的做法是去測試這個說法，而不是為自己的感覺辯護。

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to win a new car on an American TV show.
A game-show puzzle whose right answer surprises most people.
Why pigeons are better at maths than people.
How Marilyn vos Savant became a famous writer.
beginner.why: 全文：三門問題的答案違反直覺，連專家都不相信。
traps: 以偏概全：贏車只是題目設定，重點是機率。
過度推論：鴿子只是比較快學會「換門」。
以偏概全：她只是解釋答案的作者。

beginner.q: What does “that” in “The host’s choice did not change that” refer to?
options: The magazine that printed the answer in 1990.
The goat that the host showed behind door 3.
The host’s question about switching to door 2.
Your first door’s 1 in 3 chance of hiding the car.
beginner.evidence: When you first chose, you had only a 1 in 3 chance.
beginner.why: 前一句：一開始選中的機率只有三分之一，主持人開門不會改變它。
traps: 時序錯置：雜誌在第四段才出現。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：山羊是主持人打開的那扇門後的東西。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：問題是主持人提出的，不是被改變的機率。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: If you switch, you win the car two times out of three.
If you stay, you win the car two times out of three.
The host opens a door without knowing where the car is.
About 1,000 readers wrote to say Marilyn was wrong.
beginner.evidence: If you switch, you win the car two times out of three.
traps: 張冠李戴：維持原選擇只有三分之一。
正反顛倒：主持人知道車在哪裡。
數字錯位：約一萬人來信，其中近一千人有博士學位。

beginner.q: What does the writer suggest we do when a puzzle seems easy?
options: Ask someone with a PhD for the answer.
Choose the first answer that comes to mind.
Test it ourselves instead of trusting our feelings.
Keep our first choice and never switch.
beginner.evidence: When a puzzle seems easy, it is a good idea to test it.
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：近一千位博士都認為她錯了。
正反顛倒：直覺常常是錯的。
正反顛倒：文章的結論是應該換門。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Steve Selvin invented the TV game show in 1975.
Each of the two remaining doors always has a fifty-fifty chance.
Switching doors is better, though many confident people refused to believe it.
Pigeons and people solve the puzzle in exactly the same way.
intermediate.evidence: The lesson is not that people are bad at maths, but that our intuitions about probability can be confidently wrong.
intermediate.why: 全文：換門比較好，但許多人仍自信地反對。
traps: 張冠李戴：Selvin 是更早提出這個謎題的統計學家。
正反顛倒：這正是大家的錯誤直覺。
正反顛倒：鴿子很快學會換，人類卻抗拒。

intermediate.q: What does “uproar” in the fourth paragraph most likely mean?
options: A loud, angry public reaction.
A quiet agreement among readers.
A new mathematical proof.
A popular television show.
intermediate.evidence: About 10,000 readers, including nearly 1,000 with PhDs, wrote to the magazine, most of them insisting she was wrong.
intermediate.why: 一萬人來信、多數堅稱她錯了，可知是強烈的抗議聲浪。
traps: 正反顛倒：讀者多半反對她。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：證明是說服人的工具，不是這個字的意思。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：電視節目只是謎題的背景。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Vos Savant said contestants should keep their first choice.
The puzzle was first posed by Marilyn vos Savant in 1990.
The host chooses which door to open at random.
Paul Erdős changed his mind only after seeing a computer simulation.
intermediate.evidence: remained unconvinced until he was shown a computer simulation
traps: 正反顛倒：她說應該換。
時序錯置：Selvin 在 1975 年就提出過。
正反顛倒：主持人知道車在哪，刻意避開。

intermediate.q: Why does vos Savant’s million-door version make the answer easier to see?
options: It proves that every door has the same chance of hiding the car.
It shows that the one door the host leaves closed is the one he was avoiding.
It shows that the host can open the car door by mistake.
It makes the game too long for anyone to play.
intermediate.evidence: imagine a million doors, and the host opens every one except your choice and door 777,777
intermediate.why: 主持人打開其他所有門，只留下 777,777 號，這扇門顯然是他刻意避開的。
traps: 正反顛倒：機率集中到留下的那扇門。
正反顛倒：主持人一定避開車子。
過度推論：這只是思考實驗，不是要人真的玩。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To describe the history of Parade magazine.
To prove that game-show hosts always cheat contestants.
To argue that mathematicians should not trust computers.
To explain the puzzle and why our intuition fails.
advanced.evidence: The lasting lesson is that confidence is not evidence
advanced.why: 全文：三門問題的解法，以及人們為何頑固地出錯。
traps: 以偏概全：雜誌只是刊出答案的地方。
捏造：主持人的行為受規則限制，不是作弊。
正反顛倒：Erdős 正是看了電腦模擬才信服。

advanced.q: What does the author mean by saying the host’s action is “constrained”?
options: He can open any door he likes at random.
He must avoid the car and always reveal a goat.
He is not allowed to speak to the contestant.
He must open the door the contestant chose.
advanced.evidence: he knows where the car is and will never reveal it
advanced.why: 冒號後面說明：他知道車在哪、絕不會打開那扇門。
traps: 正反顛倒：他的選擇不是隨機的。
捏造：他還會問參賽者要不要換。
正反顛倒：他打開的是「沒被選的」門。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Staying with the first choice wins two-thirds of the time.
Pigeons were slower than humans to learn to switch.
Critics said the Parade version left some conditions unstated.
Steve Selvin’s letter appeared in Parade magazine.
advanced.evidence: the Parade version did not explicitly say that the host always opens a door and always offers a switch
traps: 張冠李戴：換門才是三分之二。
正反顛倒：鴿子很快學會一直換。
張冠李戴：Selvin 的信刊在 The American Statistician。

advanced.q: Why might the probabilities differ if the host could choose whether to offer a switch?
options: His choice to offer it could itself reveal information.
The car could move behind another door.
The contestant would have more doors to pick.
The goats could be replaced by cars.
advanced.evidence: if he could choose whether to do so, the probabilities might differ
advanced.why: 第四段：如果主持人能決定要不要讓你換，他的決定本身就帶有資訊。
traps: 捏造：車子不會移動。
數字錯位：門的數量不變。
捏造：獎品不會改變。

reflections: Play the game 20 times with a partner using three cups and a coin: switch 10 times and stay 10 times. What happened?
Have you ever been completely sure about something that turned out to be wrong? What helped you change your mind?

It became famous in 1990, when a reader’s version appeared in Marilyn vos Savant’s “Ask Marilyn” column in Parade magazine. A contestant chooses one of three doors, behind one of which is a car; the host, who knows where the car is, opens another door to reveal a goat and offers a chance to switch.
很少有謎題像「蒙提霍爾問題」這樣，讓這麼多聰明人吃癟。它以美國遊戲節目《來做個交易吧》的原始主持人命名，最早由統計學家塞爾文在 1975 年的一封信中提出。1990 年，讀者版本出現在《遊行》雜誌莎凡特的「問瑪莉蓮」專欄，才讓它出了名。參賽者從三扇門中選一扇，其中一扇門後有一輛汽車；知道車在哪裡的主持人打開另一扇門，露出一隻山羊，然後讓參賽者有機會換門。

Vos Savant’s answer, that the contestant should switch, provoked an extraordinary reaction. About 10,000 readers, including nearly 1,000 with PhDs, wrote to the magazine, most of them claiming she was wrong. Even when given explanations and simulations, many still refused to accept the result. The mathematician Paul Erdős reportedly remained unconvinced until he saw a computer simulation, and the argument reached the front page of The New York Times.
莎凡特的答案是參賽者應該換門，這引發了不尋常的反應。大約一萬名讀者寫信到雜誌社，其中將近一千人有博士學位，大多數都說她錯了。即使給了解釋和模擬，很多人還是拒絕接受。據說數學家艾狄胥直到看了電腦模擬才信服，這場爭論甚至登上了《紐約時報》頭版。

Under the standard assumptions, the mathematics is not difficult. The first choice has a one-third chance of being correct, so there is a two-thirds chance that the car is behind one of the other two doors. Crucially, the host’s action is constrained (limited by fixed rules): he knows where the car is and will never reveal it. By opening a losing door from the unchosen pair, he moves that entire two-thirds chance onto the remaining closed door. Switching therefore wins two times out of three; staying wins only once.
在標準假設下，數學並不難。第一次選對的機率是三分之一，所以有三分之二的機率車在另外兩扇門之一後面。關鍵在於，主持人的行動受到限制（受固定規則約束）：他知道車在哪裡，絕不會打開那扇門。他從沒被選的兩扇門中打開一扇沒獎的門，就把那整整三分之二的機率移到剩下那扇關著的門上。因此，換門三次中能贏兩次；不換只能贏一次。

Why, then, is the error so persistent? Part of the answer is that people treat the two remaining doors as equal, ignoring the information carried by the host’s choice. Another part is that the popular wording left important conditions unstated. As critics noted at the time, the Parade version did not say that the host always opens a door and always offers a switch. If he could choose whether to do so, the chances might differ.
那麼，這個錯誤為什麼這麼頑固？部分原因是，人們把剩下的兩扇門當成一樣，忽略了主持人的選擇所帶的資訊。另一部分原因是，流行的說法沒有講清楚重要的條件。當時的批評者就指出，《遊行》雜誌的版本沒有說主持人「一定」會開門、「一定」會讓人換。如果他可以選擇要不要這麼做，機率就可能不同。

Perhaps the most humbling detail comes from animal research. It is pigeons that learn quickly to always switch when they face the problem again and again, while humans tend not to. Learning from experience, the birds are untroubled by the feeling that “it must be fifty-fifty”. Not until we test such a claim, rather than defend our first feeling, do we discover how often confidence and truth part ways. The lasting lesson is simple: confidence is not evidence.
最讓人汗顏的細節，也許來自動物研究。反覆面對這個問題時，很快學會「一律換門」的是鴿子，人類卻往往學不會。從經驗中學習的鴿子，不受「一定是五五波」這種感覺困擾。直到我們去檢驗這種說法，而不是捍衛自己的第一感覺，才會發現信心和真相有多常分道揚鑣。長久的教訓很簡單：信心不是證據。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to win a car on an American game show.
A puzzle whose answer fools many people, and why it does.
Why pigeons are better at maths than mathematicians.
How Parade magazine became famous in 1990.
questions.evidence: Why, then, is the error so persistent?
questions.why: 全文：三門問題的答案、引發的爭議，以及人們為何頑固地出錯。
traps: 以偏概全：贏車只是題目設定。
